root_cause_hypothesis: RE-RUN of the 2026-08-23T09 run (sha 4203716) to verify the fix landed in 84f930a. Full BP-suppression lifecycle passes again, and the one ergonomics defect that run reported is CONFIRMED FIXED. (a) PRIMARY WITNESS -- run_bp_check finding parser. The previous run showed the structured Findings block reporting only a moniker plus a COUNT, because FINDING_LINE anchored BP...: at line start and therefore matched the per-moniker tally, never the detail line. At sha 4bb8f66 the same real xppbp.exe output now parses in full. Verbatim from this run: "Findings (moniker-checked against 577 known monikers): * BPXmlDocNoDocumentationComments (dynamics://Class/ConDemoSuppressProbe/Method/run) / path: dynamics://Class/ConDemoSuppressProbe/Method/run / Warning AxClass [(6,5),(8,6)] / No XML documentation headers are provided for ConDemoSuppressProbe.run." Severity, element type, source position, message and the dynamics:// path are all structured fields now, and the tally line is correctly dropped rather than double-reported as a second finding. The path was copied straight from that field into add-diagnostic-suppression params.diagnosticPath with no reading of raw stdout by eye and no hand reconstruction from the object name. (b) Round trip intact end to end. add-diagnostic-suppression CREATED fm-mcp_BPSuppressions.xml and its AxIgnoreDiagnosticList folder and said so; the suppressed re-run of run_bp_check went silent with NO intervening rebuild; remove-diagnostic-suppression collapsed <Items> to <Items /> (182 bytes) rather than leaving a dangling entry, and the finding came back byte-identical. A subsequent fullBuild ran "Metadata: validate ignore diagnostic list" with 0 errors, so the shape the writer stores is valid to the compiler as well as to xppbp. (c) The case-design note from the previous run is now IN the case text and held: create injected /// <summary> Executes the main processing logic. </summary> onto run(), so the first build was 0 warnings; modify/replace-code stripped it and raised the finding. Both writes stayed on the grounded path. (d) golden_match=1 on all three artifacts with zero structural deltas, so the golden captured at 4203716 is CURRENT, not stale -- the parser fix changed tool output only, not written metadata. (e) NEW, minor -- bridge declined replace-code ("Bridge error [-32603]: Error in replaceCode: oldCode not found in ConDemoSuppressProbe.run") on a multi-line oldCode carrying its leading 4-space indentation, and this server XML writer took over and applied it correctly. Self-healing and honestly reported, so not a run failure, but the bridge replaceCode matcher looks to be whitespace-sensitive in a way the XML-writer path is not. (f) NEW, minor -- eval:score has no way to carry a BP finding. --bp-warnings takes a COUNT, so the record was written with bpWarnings: [{}] and the finding detail had to be patched in by hand. Now that run_bp_check emits structured findings, the CLI could take --bp-findings <json> and keep the corpus self-describing.
suggested_fix_area: 1) NONE for the primary defect -- src/tools/sdlc/runBpCheck.ts FINDING_DETAIL_PATTERN (L244) plus the locus splitter (L246-L253) fix it; this run is the live confirmation the eval loop was waiting for. Consider adding this exact captured line as a unit-test fixture so the regex cannot regress without CI noticing. 2) src/eval/oracle/cli.ts: accept --bp-findings <file.json> (or let --bp-warnings take a path) so structured findings land in the record instead of [{}]. 3) Bridge replaceCode: normalise leading whitespace before matching oldCode, or state the normalisation in the op-spec, so the bridge path is not skipped for a correct multi-line snippet. 4) Still open from the previous run: this golden embeds the model name in both the filename and <Name> (fm-mcp_BPSuppressions), so it will not resolve under a differently named sandbox without model-name canonicalisation in artifactKey/normalize.
